items.title: GTA 6 changes the way you steal cars: here's everything you need to know about slim jims, key cloners, and tracking devices
items.summary:
Used to be that all you needed to steal a car in a GTA game was a few seconds and a sharp elbow. In GTA 6 , you can still smash a window and hotwire some cars, but the car stealing system has changed a lot and the further you get into the game, the more tools you'll need.

That means a quick getaway in a stolen vehicle isn't always that simple. Here are the methods for stealing cars, the new tools you'll get and when they become available in the story, and everything else you need to know about boosting rides in GTA 6.

Breaking into cars 

(Image credit: Rockstar Games) Want to steal a car? Walk up to the door and press the interact button. That'll tell you if it's locked (most are), if it's alarmed (nearly all are), and if it's keyless—a new type of car that we'll cover more below.

If you smash the window, you'll then climb into the car and need to hotwire it, which just takes a second or two and uses the control sticks to find the "sweet spot." If it's a keyless car, you won't be able to hotwire it or drive it away—again, more on that below. If you smash a window on an alarmed car, the alarm will sound, which can attract attention.

Carjacking You can still pull people out of their cars, but be warned: many of them will fight back, meaning you'll need to hammer a button quickly to defeat them. Lose, and they'll clonk your head against the side of the car, knocking you down and speeding away. And even if you do pull them out of their car, this is Leonida: a lot of motorists are armed and aren't shy about opening fire.

You can't slim jim a car someone is already sitting…

Reposting ProtoANZ's message, Bluepanda added , "For nearly 7 years I've been repeatedly told that my work is valued and appreciated only to then have the same people saying those things turn around and either completely ghost me or tell me they're going in a different direction with talent and that my services aren't needed GG."

items.title: How to get a snap gun in GTA 6
items.summary:
Traditional lockpicking gets an upgrade in GTA 6 with the introduction of the snap gun —a handy little device that makes picking locks faster and quieter. It's perfect for those scenarios where you don't want Jason and Lucia to set off alarms by kicking open locked doors and making demands. Instead, the snap gun offers a stealthier way through locked doors. 

Unfortunately, it's locked behind story progression like the slim jim and key cloner , so you can't make those earlier missions easier. If you don't mind a small spoiler, here's how to get the snap gun in GTA 6. 

How to get a snap gun Rockstar Rockstar You get the snap gun from Yasmani in Chapter 3 after completing the jewelry heist in the Dubious Provenance mission . Approach a locked door with the tool equipped, and the "Use snap gun" option will appear. Use the left analogue stick to find the lock's sweet spot, then press the right trigger until the meter fills. Voilà, you're in. While the snap gun circumvents alarms, the alarm itself is still active. It may still be set off by kicking open other doors, breaking display cases, or by a store employee. Using the snap gun on an establishment's back door is a great way to get access to the office to completely disable the alarm altogether.

items.title: 'I just hope GTA 6 is the last of its kind': Warren Spector congratulates Rockstar on its landmark accomplishment but says the industry can't keep this up
items.summary:
Game industry legend Warren Spector retired in August , and somewhat ironically he's been more outspoken than ever about the state of the games industry. After blowing up over the closure of BioWare in October, he took a few weeks to think about it and got even more pissed off —and now he's shared some thoughts on the biggest videogame release of all time, Grand Theft Auto 6 .

Unlike the BioWare mess, Spector's not angry about GTA 6, but he's clearly ambivalent: His latest missive on LinkedIn opens with a congratulations to the dev team and says, "It looks like it will be a high point of sorts for our medium and our business," which right out of the gate suggests that he's not entirely upbeat about it.

Spector wasted no time getting to the point. "Its billion-dollar development cost and an undoubtedly crazy marketing budget don't represent a business model anyone else can or probably should emulate," he wrote. "That's especially true when thousands of developers are out of work. A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries.

"Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is."

At the same time, he said GTA 6 demonstrates the truth of a point he's made previously: "Give a game the time and money to prove its potential (key word, potential) and you have a chance of making something great. Underfund a game or force it out the door before it's ready guaranteed failure no matter how much potential it has."

items.title: How to clone keys in GTA 6
items.summary:
Vice City's glow-up in GTA 6 ushers in a new era of smart car tech, bringing keyless ignition to the series. That's great for car owners, but a pain for our criminal duo since you can't hotwire a keyless car. Luckily, that doesn't mean you can't steal a car with high-tech security. Modern problems call for modern crimes, and that's where the key cloner comes in. 

How to get a key cloner 

(Image credit: Rockstar) You get the key cloner in Chapter 3 during the "Steal the Zorruso for Randy" mission . It's pretty far into GTA 6, but the convenience of stealing keyless cars is worth the wait. To unlock a keyless car, stand next to the vehicle's door, press the interact button, and select "Clone Key." Use the control stick to find the sweet spot to speed up the process. The key cloner unlocks and starts keyless cars, making it a serious upgrade over the slim jim while also introducing a new problem: trackers. The Waink It app on your phone can identify keyless cars when you scan them, so you'll know what you're up against. Beware of trackers when stealing keyless cars 

(Image credit: Rockstar) Standard trackers on stolen cars aren't much of a problem—they just forbid you from making modifications at a mod shop unless you register the car as your own.

Advanced trackers , however, are a whole other beast. They relay your exact location to the cops, but you can outrun the signal if you're fast enough. Keep your foot on the gas, and the cops won't be able to track you until you slow down. Apparently, the solution to beat high-tech surveillance is still a good ol' fashioned…

items.title: How to get safe codes in GTA 6
items.summary:
GTA 6 safe codes will let you unlock sealed loot containers in the main story, but also during the lucrative robbery activity, which sees you knock over gang hideouts, banks, and other cash and contraband rich institutions.

The safe codes you need in the main story or specific missions are given to you, but in order to get a safe code during a robbery (and you'll need to because they're randomised), you have two main options:

Find the code written down on the premises Interrogate an employee to get it First off, you can sometimes find the code written on something inside the store or bank, like a note on a board in the back office perhaps, or maybe a guard you've incapacitated is carrying it—press L3 and R3 to activate Focus Mode and help you find it.

You can also get the code by interrogating employees. Aim your weapon at them and use the "Threaten" or "Safe Code?" prompt shown on the screen to force them to give you the information. In certain robberies, this will also force cashiers to empty the register, as in previous GTA games.

Once you have the safe code, it will appear in the lower right corner of the screen when you're interacting with the safe. You'll have to enter the four-digit code to unlock it.

Time is of the essence, so the faster you can get the code, the quicker you can open the safe and load the cash into your bag. You can tell if an establishment has a safe by selecting it on your map, which will also give you some idea of the security level (low to high) and the approximate value of the goods, so you can pick a lucrative target for your next stick…
items.t: How to get safe codes in GTA 6

items.title: How to get a slim jim in GTA 6

Found your GTA 6 dream car but don't want to smash its windows? Or maybe you'd rather discreetly snag a getaway vehicle without setting off an alarm. There are plenty of ways to steal a car in GTA 6, and a slim jim is one of the more civilized options. 

How to get a slim jim You get the slim jim from Moses during Chapter 2's mission of the same name: Moses . It's just after Lucia goes shopping and makes a friend in the Girls' Trip mission. To use the tool, approach a car and select 'slim jim' to trigger a short sequence. You'll need to find the sweet spot with the analog stick for a second before the door pops open. Rockstar Rockstar Unlocking a car with a slim jim also lets you pop the trunk without setting off an alarm, and you might find some goodies in car trunks like weapons, drugs, or cash.

Remember that unlocking the car is only half the battle. A slim jim won't start a car with keyless ignition, but some vehicles only need to be unlocked before you can hotwire them and drive off. Keyless cars are another can of worms, requiring a key cloner .

items.title: How to get a parachute in GTA 6: Buy before you fly
items.summary:
When everything's gone sideways at 3000ft you're going to need a parachute in GTA 6. Skyscraper diving is actually what got me into playing GTA 4 online with my friends so I'm definitely buckling in for some high altitude gliding in GTA 6. Here's how to sail the skies in Leonida.

Where to get a parachute Find parachutes on a rack in an Ammu-Nation store. Rockstar You can re-equip a parachute here too if you've used yours recently. Rockstar You can buy a parachute at Ammu-Nation locations that sell clothes, indicated by the shirt icon on the map. Some skyscrapers have a box of parachutes waiting for you on the roof. You only need to buy a parachute one time, but you may need to reset it between uses. Head to a gun store and select it from the rack to add it back to your inventory before you go skydiving again. You can also just re-equip a parachute that you find on top of a skyscraper.

items.title: How to reach 6 stars in GTA 6
items.summary:
Achieving six stars in GTA 6 's new wanted system is the most notoriety you can get in the game, and killing enough cops and soldiers to get there will likely have a big impact on your criminal profile —which is effectively this game's version of Red Dead Redemption 2's karma system.

As with the previous games, the highest star levels are reserved for trespassing in an airport and stealing a passenger jet, or heading to a military base and hijacking an APC. And, as always, five stars will see a tank dispatched.

But you can only get to six stars if you cause mass destruction and loss of life. The only way we were able to get a six star wanted level in GTA 6 was by stealing a tank from a military base and blowing up other tanks and vehicles. 

Just keep this in mind:

At six stars, you'll no longer be able to lose heat or wanted level. You can run but you can't hide because once you're at six stars, the law will never stop hunting you. This means your only way out is to die, essentially. It's also worth considering that killing all of those cops could impact your criminal profile quite severely.

items.title: Ex-Take Two boss believes that attitudes towards AI in game development will change for the better: 'We are one Toy Story moment away from consumer acceptance of AI'
items.summary:
AI has been worming its way into our everyday lives for years now, although it feels like an absolute age. If I had a nickel for everytime I heard a tech bro tell us that AI is inevitable so we should all get on board, I'd have enough money to buy back all the RAM they've taken from me. So with this in mind it's hardly surprising that yet another former game exec has come out with this exact line once again. 

Ex-Take Two boss Ben Feder, who oversaw games like Red Dead Redemption and Grand Theft Auto 4 , has discussed with The Game Business how one day people will accept AI—it's just a matter of time. 

(Image credit: Rockstar) "When animation went from hand-drawn to computer animation, there was a massive wall of resistance," he says. "People didn’t think it looked good. Then Pixar launched Toy Story. They created a movie that not only was awesome, but used computer-generated animation and chose a subject matter that made the most of it, and did an amazing job with it.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling
items.summary:
I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth , the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning.

Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down.

items.title: Wooting admits 'We found an issue with the Large Knob…'

Well, Wooting opened up preorders for its $40/£34 Lekker Knob Large this year and the 80HE+ , which was expected to launch in 2026, has now been pushed back to 2027. Big news, I know. 

In a video titled " We found an issue with the Large Knob… ", Wooting co-founder and CEO Calder Limmen announced that the Large Knob has been delayed by at most four months (it has moved back to March, 2027). 

Limmen says he wanted to ship in December but "at the same time, I also had to make a decision and delay the Large Knob so that we don't ship a Large Knob with issues". 

Limmen says 30% of the Large Knobs have a defect and they don't know why. They reportedly had a torque issue where larger production batches couldn't get the same level of resistance from each knob, which was then fixed by mounting the ball bearing inside the knob differently and changing some internals. items.title: I have double-checked and yes, original 'GTA killer' Driv3r really was that rubbish
items.summary:
At this point the tragedy of Driv3r , or Driver 3, or my personal favourite Drive-thrur, is well thumbed. A familiar litany of unrealised ambition, heinous bugs, dull open-world design, and an expensive yet audibly bored voice cast, the accidental comedic highlight of which is Michelle Rodriguez flatly reeling off car theft orders from what sounds like the inside of a Michelle Rodriguez-sized tupperware container.

A more widely forgotten detail is that, for a while, there was a non-zero chance - a belief, even - that Drive Three Er was going to be the opposite. The 2003-2004 hype cycle had sowed the notion that this would in fact be the open-world crime thriller to knock Grand Theft Auto off its perch, and even 22 years before GTA 6 's idolising reviews , that was no small promise; Rockstar were still enjoying the balmy success of Vice City, and we could see San Andreas cresting the hill on a stolen, shining BMX. "Ah, but did they have Michael Madsen doing doughnuts in car parks?," publishers Atari asked the world, either unaware or in denial of the spluttering, clapped-out rattletrap they were about to wheel into the showroom.

You likely know the rest, though one of the dangers of familiarity is the subsequent breeding of complacency, which in this case can manifest as a thawing acceptance. I succumbed to this myself, having recently installed a legally unlinkable copy of Drivethreeuh, mind opened to the possibility that maybe it wasn't that bad. Six hours later, I am here to tell you: it was.

From what we're already seeing of Grand Theft Auto 6 on console, it's boding very well for a future PC release. It might only be targeting 30 fps on console, but with how stable that is and with the graphics looking so stunning on older PS5/PS5 Pro hardware, I've got high hopes for how it might run on our gaming PCs.

Digital Foundry (DF) has taken one for the team here by doing some performance testing on an inferior platform (cheap shot, I'm sorry). And judging from the screenshots, videos, and frame rate analysis so far, GTA 6 looks very much next-gen in terms of scale, scope, and fidelity.

We're talking fine detail on the local scale combined with open, bustling sight lines to the horizon, depending on your vantage point. All very noticeably saturated by incredible ray traced lighting, and running at a stable 30 fps on the PS5 Pro.

Graphics 

(Image credit: Digital Foundry @ YouTube, Rockstar Games) It's hard to describe how fantastic GTA looks. It does seem like a new era for open world games.

What particularly impresses me, judging from DF's gameplay and graphics shots, is how seamlessly fine detail combines with great lighting and breaks into long distance views. 

One minute you're inside a bustling store, with incredibly realistic ambient lighting and reflections thanks to the ray tracing implementation (plus ray traced shadows on the PS5 Pro), admiring the stranded hair on all the NPCs and the little touches such as drinks actually draining in the bottle you drink from. 

The next, you can be looking across the entire city without losing any noticeable detail.…

But the issue of how big studios are able to balance their budget still stands. “Around content, AAA is under the most amount of threat," former Take-Two CEO, Ben Feder says in an interview with The Game Business . "They’re not big enough to really be platforms on the one hand, and they’re not small enough to really innovate on the other. If you talk to the major publishers, they cannot figure out a way to make a game for less than $300 million, and that to me is just not sustainable."

(Image credit: Rockstar) We now know for sure that GTA 6 is a winner: just look at this review score round up . But there are some worried that replicating this success is nigh impossible for any other studio. As Feder puts it, not everyone can take their "entire development team, putting them in a time capsule, burying them in the ground, and five years later they pop out and say, 'Voila, here it is.'" Most studios simply do not have the capacity or funds to have a team solely working on a project for around a decade.

items.title: GTA 6 Uses FSR 4.1 on Xbox Series S to Upscale From 720p to 1080p
items.summary:
GTA 6 is finally here, and it's genuinely a technical marvel on all of the consoles it's running on. It's particularly impressive that the Xbox Series S can even run the thing, and now we know a bit more about how Rockstar was able to pull it off. 

Rather than rendering the game at the console's native 1440p, Rockstar used AMD's FSR 4.1 to upscale from 720p to 1080p, according to an interview with Wccftech . That would make GTA 6 one of the first games to use the new upscaling tech on Xbox, and it's probably what made the game possible on the budget console. 

I've already spent a bit of time with the Xbox Series S version of GTA 6, and while it does look a bit rough around the edges (literally), it looks better than I was expecting. Objects in the game are still incredibly detailed, but the edges of some objects – particularly distant buildings and hair – have a noticeable sheen of aliasing around them. But that lower resolution rendering is what lets the game mostly sit at around 30 fps (though I did notice a couple drops down to the mid-20s.)

According to the interview, though, the Xbox Series S is the only version of the game that's running on FSR 4. Both the Xbox Series X and base PS5 versions of the game are instead using Rockstar's in-house TAA (temporal anti-aliasing) solution, and the PS5 Pro is using PSSR 2.0. It shouldn't be surprising either, that the Xbox Series S is also running at the lowest input resolution out of all of the consoles at 720p, compared to 1440p on all of the other consoles.

The Xbox Series S obviously doesn't have the same graphics treats that the PS5 Pro version of the game has, but even without the ray traced shadows and the PSSR, the game holds up well on the 1440p machine. GTA 6 has become the joint-highest rated game of all time, following the widespread publication of reviews in the past hour. 

Rockstar's masterpiece currently sits with an all-time best score of 99 on Metacritic , an honor shared only with Nintendo's original The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time release back in 1997 on N64, almost 30 years ago. While both the N64 version of Ocarina and GTA 6 share a 99 average, GTA 6 has impressively managed to pull this off with more than six times' the number of reviews — over 120 at the time of writing, with over 100 of those listed with a perfect score. And while it's possible GTA 6's ranking could still slip down a point as more reviews are published, it would still be the best-rated game in nearly three decades.

Few others titles released in the recent memory have come anywhere close to this — though if you head back to the last console generation, Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Super Mario Odyssey both managed a 97 average, a standing they share with Rockstar's own Red Dead Redemption 2.

items.title: GTA 6 Doesn’t Let You Replay Story Missions — Here’s Why

GTA 6 is a little different from other games in the series, though. Its story flows and branches in small and big ways in a fluid manner not quite seen in any of the developer’s other open worlds. I’ve only completed one full playthrough myself, but can confirm that whole missions can play out differently based on decisions you didn’t even necessarily know you were making hours earlier. For example, one of GTA 6’s best missions, a daring high-stakes heist, can go relatively smoothly or turn out to be a much messier operation. 

What’s most exciting is that, now knowing this, I’m left wondering how many new things I’ll see in the second playthrough I’ve just started, as much as I am looking forward to replaying the missions I can’t easily access. items.title: GTA 6: How The Ultimate Edition Content Works
items.summary:
Ever since pre-orders for GTA 6 went live and its $100 Ultimate Edition was revealed, one question has been asked more than any other: Is it worth it?

Well, if our poll ran at the time is any indication, 70% of you certainly felt that way, with the majority opting for the full GTA 6 experience over the standard version. 

We’ve long known what is included in the more expensive edition, from personalised vehicles and weapons to exclusive stores and missions. But what we didn’t know was how exactly we’d access this extra stuff or when we’d be able to use it. Well, now we do, thanks to the details listed in the in-game store, which states, “Ultimate Edition bonuses are threaded across all aspects of Jason and Lucia’s Story, with new items uncovered behind each chapter”.

It turns out that these extras will be sprinkled throughout the story, unlocking over the course of its chapters, with some only being available to use during certain timeframes, and even permanently removing your access to them once you pass points in Jason and Lucia’s tale.

items.title: GTA 6 Photo Mode Confirmed at Launch
items.summary:
GTA 6 is a gorgeous-looking game, so naturally, you’ll feel the urge to pause regularly to take it all in. Thankfully, Rockstar knows this and has included a full-fledged photo mode at launch.

The developer is no stranger to such a concept, with GTA 5 including a whole movie director mode, and Red Dead Redemption 2 eventually gaining a photo mode alongside its PC launch. It’s a pleasant surprise, then, that it's here from the get-go with GTA 6.

It took 70 hours to complete my first playthrough of Jason and Lucia’s story, but I’d be lying if I said a couple of those hours weren’t spent messing around taking pictures when the mood struck me. Sometimes the light bounces perfectly off those waters off Ocean Beach, and you just can’t help but capture the moment.

The photo studio, found by pausing the game and hitting the square button on PS5/X button on Xbox, is impressively well-equipped, too. With aspect ratios, aperture, and depth of field all available to play with when it comes to the camera itself, a variety of different lighting from spotlights to floodlights to softboxes all available to insert into scenes, and a range of post-processing tools including a variety of filters, it’s a relatively impressive suite that I’ve enjoyed playing around with.

That being said, there are a few little things here and there that I’d love to see Rockstar introduce in future updates. Perhaps the primary one of those is the ability to reposition Jason and Lucia into new poses and change their facial expressions. Sometimes you just get that perfect background scenery, but unfortunately…
items.t: GTA 6 Photo Mode Confirmed at Launch

items.title: GTA 6 Switches Sprint to L3, Saving Thumbs Globally
items.summary:
Ever since Grand Theft Auto made the switch to 3D space with 2001’s GTA 3 , players have had to make use of the X button on PlayStation or the A button on Xbox to sprint. Up until San Andreas , holding down the relevant face button would trigger sprint, but CJ’s story changed that to just meaning “run”, with a repeated tap introduced for a full-fledged sprint. It’s been that way ever since with Rockstar’s games, including most recently 2018’s Red Dead Redemption 2 , leaving sore thumbs globally at the end of long chase sequences.

Well now, with GTA 6 , everything has changed.

Finally, Rockstar’s return to Vice City changes the default sprint button to a press of the left analog stick, with a click of L3 making both Jason and Lucia sprint easily. You get the sense that the developer knows what a big deal this is, too, with one of the very first screens you see when first booting up GTA 6 being a warning about this change, alongside a message letting you know you can revert back to a more classic control scheme if you like.

Interestingly, in a fun little easter egg of sorts, there is one instance you’ll have to run where the traditional button mapping does return. In a nod to the series’ past, if you use a treadmill at one of the map’s several gyms, the minigame asks you to repeatedly press down the X/A button at the correct rhythm to score as high as possible. So, if you fancy getting either of the protagonists in great shape, you’ll also be giving your thumb a workout at the same time.

items.title: How Long is GTA 6?

In every sense of the word, Grand Theft Auto 6 is a massive game. But just how much time will you have to set aside to see all of it? Well, that could potentially take years given the size of its map and the incredible amount of detail packed into it – we’re still exploring to find its many hidden secrets, hours after finishing the main mission chain. What we can give you an idea of, though, is just how long it took us to finish the story.

We’ve gathered playtimes from four different writers from across IGN and our sister websites, Eurogamer and Pure Xbox , in order to showcase just how much that hour total can vary. Here’s how long it took us to beat GTA 6, the playstyles each player opted for, and what they prioritised their time doing.

How Long is Grand Theft Auto 6? Our fastest player finished GTA 6 in 42 hours. Our “slowest” player took 115 hours to see the credits roll. Everyone plays games differently, so read on for more details about how everyone played, how long it took to reach the credits, and some of their unique thoughts about the game's length. Countless GTA 6 fans are expected to take advantage of the cheeky Xbox loophole where you can quickly switch your console to another region and gain access to new releases slightly earlier. GTA 6 doesn't officially launch until midnight wherever you are... well, it is midnight earlier in New Zealand than likely wherever you're ready this. (Unless you are in New Zealand, in which case, hello!)

Hilariously, the New Zealand trick has become so popular that the country itself is now acknowledging it, as well as the numerous GTA 6 owners who will be playing from the home of hobbits and the haka, for a few hours today at least.

"One perk of seeing the sun first? Getting GTA 6 first too," reads a post on the New Zealand tourist board's Instagram account. "We heard a few of you are trying the New Zealand trick to join us. We get it, and we'd love to have you."

While the New Zealand trick is perfectly safe, it is technically not what the Xbox's region settings were originally designed for. Still, Microsoft has always kept quiet about the manoeuvre — and likely will continue to do so as it seeks every advantage it can take over PlayStation, where the vast majority of GTA 6 copies are expected to be sold.

You can do a version of the New Zealand trick on PS5, but it's more fiddly and there are more hoops to jump through. We've got a breakdown of the New Zealand trick right here if you fancy giving it a shot .

items.title: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success
items.summary:
It's bizarre today to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't Grand Theft Auto . Frankly, it's bizarre to think of Rockstar working on games that aren't GTA 6 , which rolls onto console hard drives this week. A decade in the making, with a development team of thousands scattered across an international network of studios, GTA 6 aims to be the Maximum Game. It's both a dense, lively open world and a monument to the exhausting impersonality of "triple-A" game productions. It contains multitudes: birdlife! Realistic cloud formation! Fuel mechanics! Romance! Soda visibly sloshing around in bottles! It's an imperial production shadowed by labour disputes , that appears to have given Rockstar's various teams little time or space to think about anything else.

It wasn't ever thus. Once upon a time, Rockstar weren't just known for GTA and to a considerably lesser extent, Red Dead Redemption . Once upon a time, they had a reputation for slightly dodgy experiments. I recently interviewed former Rockstar North tech director Obbe Vermeij about a few of them, including Agent, the unofficial James Bond game Rockstar toyed with before putting all chips on Grand Theft Auto 5 .
items.t: What would Rockstar have done if GTA hadn't taken off? Former tech director Obbe Vermeij on Scottish zombies, James Bond and the "curse" of success

items.title: "Games are best made by people": The IWGB and other European unions publish joint manifesto calling on workers, employers and consumers to reject genAI
items.summary:
As part of a summit meeting in Manchester yesterday, the IWGB Game Workers union have joined up with other unions spanning the Republic of Ireland's GWUI, Germany's GDRT, Italy's FIOM-CGIL, France's STJV, and Spain's CSVI to publish a manifesto that aims to "bring to light the risks and dangers genAI poses to the workforce" for consumers, workers and publishers alike.

The manifesto states that "GenAI is currently harming the games industry, its workers and the games they produce," and suggests actions that can be taken by all to reduce harm done to the industry. The manifesto specifies the "severe harm to the environment, the destruction of communities and the exploitation of the Global South" as wider harms of the technology, but maintains its focus on the industry itself.

items.title: Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics
items.summary:
It's amazing what a difference a few lines of preamble can make to your understanding of a game. Out now on PC, Steel Gullet is a factory engineering puzzler that, while notable for its meticulous interest in thermodynamics, broadly compares to the foundational work of Zachtronics , together with more recent and focussed conveyor belt wranglers such as Modulus . Resources come in, and you arrange machines on a grid to transform them into something else, before sliding them into an output hopper.

The difference is that you're doing this inside a huge walking fortress city, which stamps across the surface of a largely unseen, devastated and uninhabitable Earth. Your resources are the refuse of a bygone human civilisation: knots of concrete and rebar, flaccid rubber hose and splintered plank, that must be separated out before you can manufacture anything.
items.t: Break up and re-commodify a fallen Earth in Steel Gullet, a satisfyingly funereal factory puzzler that really loves thermodynamics
